content.text:
Entire Review: [Trail 1197](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1197) / [PR #2209](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2209)

The implementation is substantial and CI is green, but I found three issues worth addressing before calling Codex support complete.

### Findings

- **High — fallback discovery can repeatedly read every Codex transcript in full.**  
  [`codex.go`](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/863faec50347dbef7c090dd491e75f6279fdf27e/cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/codex.go#L139-L202) traverses active and archived rollouts and calls `io.ReadAll` for every JSONL whenever a child lacks a resolved path. That is a normal state for a running background subagent, so parent turn hooks can repeatedly perform an unbounded scan. Inspect only the first metadata line for unrelated candidates, read full contents only for matching IDs, and impose a hook-safe budget.

- **Medium — cross-agent state correction permanently loses exact Codex totals.**  
  [`manual_commit_hooks.go`](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/863faec50347dbef7c090dd491e75f6279fdf27e/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go#L2525-L2536) can correct an existing session to Codex, but its Codex inventory markers remain unset. On the next load, normalization marks them incomplete; nothing promotes them again, so exact child totals remain unavailable. Add initialization for a verified transition to Codex and a regression test covering the documented multi-hook race.

- **Medium — `--ephemeral` behavior contradicts the Codex documentation.**  
  A null `transcript_path` is classified as unknown, causing both [TurnStart and TurnEnd to be discarded](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/863faec50347dbef7c090dd491e75f6279fdf27e/cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/lifecycle.go#L206-L305), while `AGENT.md` says ephemeral transcripts are handled gracefully. This means no usable lifecycle tracking in that mode. It needs either an authoritative root/child discriminator that works without a transcript, or an explicit unsupported-mode contract and test.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Codex needs more than start/stop hooks: accurate tracking depends on a durable child inventory, verified rollout identity, terminal-turn evidence, and exact cumulative token snapshots. Losing any one of those should degrade completeness, but should not make ordinary hooks unbounded.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

### Missing smoke-test session

I found a strong candidate:

- Session: `01a0352f-4475-7981-bf5c-8f110df6207d`
- Checkpoint: `01M0TMA73H07416XNTHJRR2BXB`
- Created: August 24, 2026
- Agent: Codex
- File: `testdata/subagent-tracking/parent-committed.txt`
- Recorded branch: `subagents`

Unfortunately, the checkpoint has **no stored transcript**, and `entire session info` no longer finds the live session record. It therefore cannot be replayed or resumed through Entire, although it is very likely related to your smoke testing.

The current trail’s actual branch is `feat/codex-subagent-tracking`, not `subagents`. That branch has no local worktree/ref and `entire trail resume` reports no attached sessions or checkpoints. The PR head object is present locally at `863faec50347dbef7c090dd491e75f6279fdf27e`, so the code can be reconstructed into a worktree, but not the lost conversation. I made no local mutations.

### Broader agent-parity goal

The merged precedents establish the intended architecture:

- [PR #1958](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1958): initial Codex subagent hooks.
- [PR #2032](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2032): durable background-subagent capture.
- [PR #2034](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2034): commits made mid-task linked to the parent session.
- [PR #1710](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1710): cumulative transcript extraction and token accounting fixes.

Current parity is still uneven:

| Agent | Current subagent coverage |
|---|---|
| Claude Code / Droid | Strong lifecycle and transcript extraction |
| Codex | This PR adds robust thread-spawned tracking; internal/synthetic subagents remain invisible |
| Cursor | Start/stop lifecycle, but not equivalent token/inventory reconciliation |
| Copilot CLI | Stop-only; no authoritative start |
| Gemini / OpenCode / Pi | No equivalent first-class subagent lifecycle |

Trail automation currently reports no open findings: six resolved and one dismissed. Every GitHub CI job passes. The PR remains a draft and `Entire Gates` is red only because it has no approval; it is `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, not merge-ready.

No code was changed or tests run during this read-only review. I can next produce a concrete fix plan for these three findings and an agent-by-agent parity roadmap, or reconstruct the PR branch into a local worktree.

Recommended approach: surgical fixes on PR #2209, preserving its existing architecture.

Alternatives considered:

1. **Surgical fixes — recommended.** Optimize rollout lookup, repair Codex state promotion, and define truthful ephemeral behavior. Lowest review risk.
2. **Persistent rollout index.** Faster lookup, but adds cache invalidation and migration complexity beyond these findings.
3. **Trust hook-provided paths only.** Simpler, but fails for delayed/background subagents and weakens identity verification.

Proposed design:

- Recover `feat/codex-subagent-tracking` locally at PR head `863faec…`.
- Add failing regression tests first for:
  - metadata-only scanning of unrelated rollouts;
  - a session corrected from another agent to Codex;
  - null/unknown Codex transcript handling.
- Change fallback discovery to read only `session_meta` from unrelated files, then fully load only exact child-ID matches, with a bounded scan.
- Initialize Codex inventory completeness during an authoritative agent-type correction, while keeping genuinely legacy/partial sessions conservative.
- Make ephemeral behavior explicit and non-corrupting: preserve session lifecycle where possible, skip transcript-dependent checkpoint creation with a clear diagnostic, and update tests/docs to match.
- Run focused tests, `mise run check`, then build/install the local CLI into an isolated environment.
- Create a disposable Git repository, enable Entire for Codex, run a real Codex prompt that delegates a file change to a subagent, commit as an end user, and inspect the resulting session/checkpoint for:
  - parent session identity;
  - child inventory and finalized turn;
  - child-modified file inclusion;
  - complete, non-duplicated token totals;
  - checkpoint explainability.
- No real-agent E2E matrix—only the explicitly requested Codex smoke test.

+# Codex Subagent Tracking Hardening Design
+
+## Goal
+
+Close the three manual-review findings on PR #2209 and prove the resulting
+behavior through a real Codex session in an isolated repository, using the CLI
+as an end user would.
+
+## Constraints
+
+- Preserve exact child identity verification: a rollout is accepted only when
+  it is a regular file and its first `session_meta.id` equals the observed
+  Codex `agent_id`.
+- Preserve conservative token semantics. Missing or ambiguous child evidence
+  must clear aggregate child tokens rather than estimate them.
+- Keep hook execution bounded enough that a large Codex history cannot stall a
+  turn or session lifecycle event.
+- Do not use the CLI repository itself as smoke-test data. Build the candidate
+  CLI and exercise it in a disposable Git repository.
+- The real Codex invocation is explicitly authorized. Other paid-agent E2E
+  suites remain out of scope.
+
+## Design
+
+### Rollout discovery
+
+Split fallback discovery into metadata inspection and full rollout loading.
+For each JSONL candidate, open and verify the regular file, read only the first
+record needed to extract `session_meta.id`, and discard unrelated candidates
+without loading the remaining transcript. Candidates whose IDs are requested
+are then read completely from the same verified descriptor. Continue scanning
+all configured roots so duplicate IDs remain ambiguous and therefore rejected.
+
+Bound fallback work with a context-aware or explicit scan budget appropriate
+for lifecycle hooks. A budget breach returns incomplete extraction, preserving
+the current fail-closed accounting behavior. Direct declared/resolved paths
+remain the fast path.
+
+### Agent-type correction
+
+When an existing session is authoritatively corrected to Codex from its
+transcript path, initialize Codex inventory markers deliberately instead of
+letting load-time legacy migration mark the session permanently incomplete.
+A fresh state with no prior child evidence starts complete. A state that may
+already contain child/task evidence remains incomplete unless completeness can
+be proven. Clear stale aggregate child totals whenever the ownership model
+changes.
+
+### Null and unclassified transcripts
+
+Do not let an absent Codex transcript impersonate a child rollout, and do not
+claim transcript-backed checkpoint support where no transcript exists. Preserve
+safe session-level lifecycle behavior for confirmed root events when possible;
+transcript-dependent turn finalization must skip with a clear diagnostic rather
+than corrupting root state. Keep confirmed child rollouts excluded from root
+lifecycle handling. Update Codex documentation so `--ephemeral` behavior is
+precise and covered by tests.
+
+## Automated Testing
+
+Use red-green TDD for each finding:
+
+1. A fallback scan containing large unrelated rollouts proves that unrelated
+   bodies are not fully read, while matching rollouts retain same-file identity
+   verification and duplicate rejection.
+2. An existing non-Codex state corrected by a verified Codex transcript proves
+   inventory markers and child-token fields transition conservatively and can
+   later produce exact totals.
+3. Null, unknown, root, and child transcript classifications prove lifecycle
+   events are neither silently misclassified nor allowed to mutate the wrong
+   session.
+
+Run focused package tests after every change, then `mise run check` before any
+commit or remote update.
+
+## Real Codex Smoke Test
+
+1. Build the candidate `entire` binary.
+2. Create an isolated temporary Git repository with local user configuration
+   and an initial commit.
+3. Isolate Entire config, cache, token-store, and Codex configuration where
+   possible while retaining the authenticated Codex runtime.
+4. Enable Entire's Codex hooks using the candidate binary.
+5. Run a real writable Codex session with a prompt that requires a spawned
+   subagent to create a distinctive file, then have the parent perform a second
+   small change so the root lifecycle also completes.
+6. Commit through the normal Git workflow.
+7. Inspect `entire session`, checkpoint metadata, stored transcript/task
+   records, modified files, and token totals. The smoke test passes only if the
+   checkpoint is attached to the parent session, includes the child-created
+   file, records the child identity/terminal evidence, and reports truthful
+   child-token completeness without duplication.
+
+If Codex declines to delegate, revise only the smoke-test prompt and retry; do
+not weaken product assertions or synthesize hook payloads.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- Implementing missing subagent hooks for Gemini, OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, or
+  Copilot CLI.
+- Replacing the rollout inventory with a persistent global index.
+- Recovering the unavailable historical Codex transcript.
+- Merging the pull request.
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

# Codex Subagent Tracking Hardening Design

## Goal

Close the three manual-review findings on PR #2209 and prove the resulting behavior through a real Codex session in an isolated repository, using the CLI as an end user would.

## Constraints

- Preserve exact child identity verification: a rollout is accepted only when it is a regular file and its first `session_meta.id` equals the observed Codex `agent_id`.
- Preserve conservative token semantics. Missing or ambiguous child evidence must clear aggregate child tokens rather than estimate them.
- Keep hook execution bounded enough that a large Codex history cannot stall a turn or session lifecycle event.
- Do not use the CLI repository itself as smoke-test data. Build the candidate CLI and exercise it in a disposable Git repository.
- The real Codex invocation is explicitly authorized. Other paid-agent E2E suites remain out of scope.

## Design

### Rollout discovery

Split fallback discovery into metadata inspection and full rollout loading.

One batched traversal serves every unresolved child ID. For each JSONL candidate:

1. Open and verify that it is a regular file.
2. Read only the first record needed to extract `session_meta.id`.
3. Discard unrelated candidates without loading the remaining transcript.
4. Accept EOF as a complete first record when the file has no trailing newline.
5. Reject a first record that exceeds the metadata byte limit.
6. For requested child IDs, read the complete rollout from the same verified file descriptor.

All configured rollout roots must still be scanned so duplicate child IDs remain ambiguous and are rejected.

Add `context.Context` to the built-in-only interface method:

```go
InventoryAwareExtractor.ExtractWithSubagentInventory
```

The existing helper:

```go
agent.ExtractWithSubagentInventory(ctx, ...)
```

will pass its caller context into that method. The same context and budget will propagate through fallback traversal and rollout reading.

The fallback scan will use these explicit limits:

- 500 ms wall-clock budget for the complete fallback scan.
- 20,000 candidate JSONL files.
- 64 KiB maximum for each first metadata record.
- 128 MiB maximum for each matching rollout.
- 256 MiB maximum across all matching rollout bodies.

Replace `filepath.WalkDir` on this fallback path with an incremental directory walker built from directory handles and bounded `ReadDir(128)` batches. `filepath.WalkDir` sorts an entire directory before invoking callbacks, which prevents reliable deadline enforcement during that read.

Cancellation and deadlines will be checked:

- Between directory batches.
- Between directory entries.
- Between chunks of matching-rollout reads.

Exceeding any limit, encountering malformed candidate metadata, or losing same-file verification discards every partial fallback result. Extraction then reports incomplete child coverage.

Tests will use injected clocks and reader counters instead of sleeping. They will verify:

- Exact bytes read from unrelated candidates.
- One traversal for multiple unresolved child IDs.
- Incremental cancellation.
- Missing-newline first-record handling.
- Candidate-count enforcement.
- Per-rollout size enforcement.
- Aggregate matching-rollout size enforcement.
- Wall-clock budget enforcement.
- Complete rejection of partial results after any breach.
- Duplicate child-ID rejection.

Declared and previously resolved transcript paths remain the fast path. They retain the 128 MiB per-rollout size limit but do not pay the fallback traversal budget.

### Agent-type correction

When a verified transcript path proves that an existing session belongs to Codex, perform one atomic ownership transition.

This avoids allowing load-time legacy migration to mark a clean corrected session permanently incomplete.

“Prior child evidence” means any of the following:

- Non-empty subagent inventory.
- Non-empty task records.
- Non-zero subagent ledger version.
- A child total in session token usage.
- A child total in checkpoint token usage.
- A stored child-token baseline.
- An explicit false `TokenUsage.SubagentTokensComplete`.
- An explicit false `CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokensComplete`.
- An explicitly incomplete inventory marker.
- An explicitly incomplete baseline marker.

For a clean correction:

- Set the agent type to Codex.
- Keep the inventory empty.
- Keep the ledger version at zero.
- Clear the child-token baseline.
- Set inventory completeness to true.
- Set baseline completeness to true.
- Set `TokenUsage.SubagentTokensComplete` to true with a nil child total.
- Set `CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokensComplete` to true with a nil child total.

This represents authoritative exact-empty child coverage.

For a dirty correction:

- Preserve task records.
- Preserve the existing inventory.
- Preserve ledger identities and version.
- Backfill every non-empty task-record `AgentID` missing from the inventory.
- Clear session-level child totals.
- Clear checkpoint-level child totals.
- Clear the child-token baseline.
- Set inventory completeness to false.
- Set baseline completeness to false.
- Set `TokenUsage.SubagentTokensComplete` to false.
- Set `CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokensComplete` to false.

A dirty correction remains conservative for the lifetime of that session because missed historical child starts cannot be disproved. Only clean-correction cases may later report exact aggregate child totals.

Tests will cover:

- Clean correction from a known incorrect agent.
- Clean correction from an unknown agent.
- Dirty correction with inventory evidence.
- Dirty correction with task records but missing inventory entries.
- Dirty correction with only token completeness evidence.
- Atomic clearing of stale child totals and baselines.

### Null and unclassified transcripts

An absent or unreadable Codex transcript must not impersonate either a root or child rollout.

Lifecycle behavior remains explicitly fail-closed:

| Transcript classification | TurnStart | TurnEnd | Diagnostic |
|---|---|---|---|
| Valid root | Initialize or advance the parent session | Extract, checkpoint, and transition the parent to idle | Normal operational logs |
| Valid child | No parent mutation | No parent mutation | Debug classification only |
| Null (`--ephemeral`) | No parent mutation | No parent mutation or checkpoint | Warning in `.entire/logs`; documentation states Entire tracking is unavailable |
| Unreadable path | No parent mutation | No parent mutation or checkpoint | Warning with path and read-error category |
| Malformed first record | No parent mutation | No parent mutation or checkpoint | Warning with parsing category |
| Future or unclassified source | No parent mutation | No parent mutation or checkpoint | Warning containing the source value |

`SessionStart` may still display installation and hook-trust diagnostics, but it does not create turn state.

`SessionEnd` remains best-effort cleanup only for state that was created by a confirmed root turn.

Codex documentation will be updated to remove the inaccurate claim that `--ephemeral` sessions are tracked gracefully. The documentation will instead state that Entire cannot track ephemeral sessions because Codex supplies no transcript-backed root identity or checkpoint content.

Tests will assert:

- Parser output.
- Persisted session phase.
- Task inventory.
- Checkpoint count.
- Absence of unintended parent mutations.
- Diagnostic category.

These assertions will cover every row in the lifecycle matrix, not merely the classification helper’s return value.

## Automated Testing

Each finding will follow red-green TDD.

### Rollout scanning

A fallback scan containing large unrelated rollouts will prove that unrelated bodies are not fully read.

Matching rollouts must retain:

- Same-file identity verification.
- Exact `session_meta.id` matching.
- Duplicate rejection.
- Complete-body analysis within the configured limits.

The test suite will also verify all scan budgets and multi-ID batching.

### Agent correction

Existing known and unknown non-Codex states corrected by a verified Codex transcript will exercise the complete atomic transition.

Only clean corrections may subsequently produce exact child totals. Dirty corrections must:

- Backfill task-record identities.
- Clear stale totals.
- Retain durable child evidence.
- Remain explicitly incomplete.

### Transcript classification

Root, child, null, unreadable, malformed, and future/unclassified transcript cases will verify that lifecycle events are neither silently misclassified nor allowed to mutate the wrong session.

The tests will inspect persisted state and checkpoint counts.

### Repository verification

After each focused change:

1. Run the directly affected package test.
2. Confirm the new regression test fails before implementation.
3. Apply the smallest implementation change.
4. Confirm the focused test passes.
5. Run the surrounding package test suite.

Before any commit or remote update:

```bash
mise run check
```

The current baseline has two unrelated failures that must be distinguished from changes made here:

- The integration suite’s `TestMain` can wait on its spawned test binary until Go’s 11-minute timeout.
- `TestBetterleaksDoesNotPoisonGitEnvironment` constructs an invalid unquoted Go module replacement when the worktree path contains spaces.

Those failures will be reproduced separately. New Codex changes must pass their focused tests independently, and the full gate must be rerun after resolving or otherwise isolating the baseline failures.

## Real Codex Smoke Test

The final smoke test will use a real Codex process and real installed hooks. It must not call `entire hooks`, construct hook payloads, or invoke synthetic lifecycle events directly.

### Environment preparation

1. Build the candidate `entire` binary.
2. Create an isolated temporary Git repository.
3. Configure repository-local Git user identity and disable GPG signing.
4. Create an initial commit.
5. Put the candidate binary alone at the front of `PATH`.
6. Verify that both `.codex/hooks.json` and installed Git hooks resolve that exact executable.
7. Isolate:
   - Entire configuration.
   - Entire cache.
   - Entire token store.
   - Codex configuration.
8. Create an isolated `CODEX_HOME`.
9. Copy only the authenticated Codex credential material into it.
10. Do not reuse or mutate the real Codex configuration.

### Hook setup

1. Enable Entire’s Codex integration using the candidate binary.
2. Establish trust for every installed Codex hook inside the isolated `CODEX_HOME`.
3. Verify using the candidate CLI’s diagnostics that:
   - Every required hook is installed.
   - No hook drift is present.
   - No trust gaps remain.
   - The hook command resolves to the candidate binary.

### Real agent run

Run a writable real Codex session with a prompt requiring Codex to:

1. Spawn a subagent.
2. Have that subagent create a distinctive file.
3. Wait for the subagent to finish.
4. Have the parent make a separate small change.
5. Finish the root turn normally.

If Codex declines to delegate, only the smoke-test prompt may be revised and retried. Product assertions must not be weakened, and hook events must not be synthesized.

### End-user commit

After the Codex process completes:

1. Inspect the working tree as an end user.
2. Stage the changes.
3. Commit through the ordinary Git workflow.
4. Confirm that Entire attaches a checkpoint trailer.
5. Inspect the checkpoint using public CLI commands.

### Required assertions

The smoke test passes only if all of these hold:

- The checkpoint is attached to the parent Codex session.
- The parent session contains a durable child inventory entry.
- The child turn has terminal evidence.
- The checkpoint includes the child-created file.
- The materialized child task entry—not merely the parent checkpoint’s combined file list—owns the distinctive file.
- The child task entry references the verified child rollout.
- The stored child ID equals the rollout’s native `session_meta.id`.
- The stored child token total equals the child rollout’s final native cumulative token snapshot.
- Child tokens are counted exactly once.
- Reconciliation through SubagentStop, SessionEnd, and commit does not multiply the child total.
- Completeness is true only when every observed child resolves with exact terminal and token evidence.
- `entire checkpoint explain` can read the resulting checkpoint and session metadata.

## Non-goals

- Implementing missing subagent hooks for Gemini, OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, or Copilot CLI.
- Replacing the rollout inventory with a persistent global index.
- Recovering the unavailable historical Codex transcript.
- Running paid real-agent E2E suites beyond the explicitly authorized Codex smoke test.
- Merging the pull request.

The first version was smaller largely because it modeled the happy path: find a child rollout and attach it. Yes—there is meaningful avoidable complexity here. The original implementation was smaller partly because it was incomplete, but the current version also grew through patch-by-patch hardening instead of converging on a simpler architecture.

### Why it grew

The foundation commit added 1,930 lines. Everything after that added another 1,463 lines:

| Area added after foundation | Approximate growth |
|---|---:|
| Production logic | +795 |
| Tests | +668 |
| Total | +1,463 |

The latest hardening commit alone was `+960/-101`. It replaced several optimistic assumptions:

- `io.ReadAll` of arbitrary rollout files became bounded, cancellable reading.
- `filepath.WalkDir` across all active and archived Codex sessions became a resource-budgeted scanner.
- A child stop could no longer be treated as final immediately.
- One Codex child can have multiple turns and follow-ups.
- A session can end before a child’s final evidence is reconciled.
- Verified transcript paths must be copied into the durable task record.
- Child token totals need three states: exact, incomplete, and unknown.
- Sessions initially attributed to the wrong agent need careful migration.

Those are real problems caught by review and smoke testing. So the first implementation was smaller mainly because it had not yet modeled the complete Codex lifecycle.

But the fixes accumulated around the initial shape, producing duplication:

- `TaskRecords` and `SubagentInventory` now track overlapping child identity and transcript information.
- Token completeness is represented separately in multiple places with `*bool`.
- Generic lifecycle code contains several `AgentTypeCodex` branches.
- [`codex.go`](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/Documents - Peyton’s MacBook Pro/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/subagents/cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/codex.go:145>) combines secure file opening, directory walking, resource budgets, rollout resolution, and test seams.
- [`ExtractWithSubagentInventory`](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/Documents - Peyton’s MacBook Pro/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/subagents/cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/transcript.go:603>) combines parent parsing, child resolution, child parsing, aggregation, and completeness.
- The same rollout JSONL is parsed repeatedly for metadata, terminal turns, files, and usage.

### What we can reuse

A lot of the existing cross-agent framework is already appropriate:

- The normalized `SubagentStart` and `SubagentEnd` events.
- Shared subagent lifecycle handling.
- `TaskRecord` checkpoint materialization.
- Transcript sanitization, externalization, and redaction.
- The existing cumulative-child-token baseline logic.
- The exact transcript path supplied by `agent_transcript_path`.

The old [`SubagentAwareExtractor`](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/Documents - Peyton’s MacBook Pro/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/subagents/cmd/entire/cli/agent/agent.go:595>) cannot be reused directly, though. Claude and Factory Droid assume:

1. Child IDs can be rediscovered from the parent transcript.
2. Child files live under a deterministic task directory.
3. Missing child transcripts can simply be skipped.
4. Aggregated child usage is still usable when one child is unavailable.

Those assumptions are precisely what Codex cannot make. Codex has explicit hook identities and paths, but child completion and token snapshots require stricter verification.

The abstraction can be reused; the Claude/Factory implementation cannot.

### How I would design it now

I would organize it around one generic subagent ledger and one Codex evidence adapter:

```text
Codex hooks
    ↓
normalized subagent observation
    ↓
shared durable subagent ledger
    ↓
Codex evidence provider
    ├── verify declared transcript path
    ├── analyze rollout once
    └── return files, turns, usage, coverage
    ↓
shared reconciliation + checkpoint materialization
```

The important changes would be:

1. **Use one durable child ledger**

   Replace the overlapping Codex `SubagentInventory` plus `TaskRecords` model with one generic `SubagentRecord` containing:

   - child identity
   - invocation identity
   - transcript path
   - observed/finalized turns
   - materialization state
   - latest exact evidence

   Other agents could migrate to it later. Codex would no longer need to synchronize two collections manually.

2. **Generalize lifecycle capability instead of checking `AgentTypeCodex`**

   The generic lifecycle should ask whether the agent supports authoritative child reconciliation. That makes this useful for future agents and removes Codex-specific branching from [`lifecycle.go`](</Users/peytonmontei/Documents/Documents - Peyton’s MacBook Pro/entire/devenv/entireio/cli/.worktrees/subagents/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:941>).

3. **Make rollout analysis a single pure pass**

   One function should consume verified JSONL bytes and return:

   ```go
   type RolloutEvidence struct {
       ID            string
       Role          RootOrChild
       ModifiedFiles []string
       TerminalTurns []string
       Usage         *TokenUsage
       Coverage      Coverage
   }
   ```

   That replaces separate metadata, file, terminal-turn, and exact-token scans. Pure parsing is also much easier to test compactly.

4. **Use an explicit completeness type**

   Instead of `*bool` on token usage, inventory, and baselines:

   ```go
   type Coverage uint8

   const (
       CoverageUnknown Coverage = iota
       CoverageIncomplete
       CoverageComplete
   )
   ```

   Bundle coverage with the child usage snapshot. This would prevent the bugs caused by independently copying totals and completeness flags.

5. **Do not recursively scan all Codex rollouts during the normal hook path**

   Codex’s `SubagentStop` normally supplies `agent_transcript_path`. The normal flow should:

   - verify that exact path’s `session_meta.id`;
   - save it in the ledger;
   - mark evidence incomplete if it is absent or not yet readable;
   - retry at the next root stop, session end, or post-commit.

   The current global fallback scan is responsible for several hundred production and test lines. If fallback recovery is a product requirement, I would move it off the latency-sensitive hook path and make it a reusable indexed recovery component. I would not make every ordinary checkpoint walk `sessions/` and `archived_sessions/`.

6. **Extract the secure-file primitive**

   Codex already has similar `Lstat → Open → Stat → SameFile → bounded read` logic for hooks configuration. A shared internal helper could handle stable regular-file reads instead of maintaining another bespoke copy for rollouts.

7. **Make reconciliation a pure state transition**

   Something like:

   ```go
   nextState, effects := ReconcileSubagent(state, observation, evidence)
   ```

   The caller would handle locking and persistence. Tests could then express the important lifecycle cases in a compact table without repeatedly initializing Git repositories and session stores.

### What I would keep Codex-specific

I would not over-generalize these:

- Codex `session_meta` parsing.
- Root-versus-child rollout classification.
- Codex terminal-turn rules.
- Exact cumulative token snapshot extraction.
- Verification that `session_meta.id == agent_id`.
- Codex’s provisional-stop semantics.

Those are native protocol details and belong in `agent/codex`.

### Likely resulting size

A fully robust implementation probably cannot return to the original 1,930 lines—that version did not cover enough real behavior.

But I think the same reliability could reasonably land around 2,200–2,500 additions instead of 3,333:

- Remove or defer most fallback-scanner machinery: roughly 300–400 lines.
- Consolidate the state model and reconciliation: roughly 150–250 lines.
- Parse rollouts once: roughly 75–125 lines.
- Compress duplicated tests and fixtures: roughly 300–400 lines.

So approximately 800–1,100 lines of the current branch look avoidable, while the rest represents real functionality and regression protection.

My recommendation would be to refactor before merge, but not rewrite everything:

1. Make the Codex rollout analyzer single-pass.
2. Remove the recursive fallback scan from normal hooks, unless we explicitly decide it is a required guarantee.
3. Introduce a generic reconciliation capability to eliminate Codex type checks.
4. Consolidate the test suite.
5. Treat full ledger unification and the coverage enum as either part of this PR if we accept wire-format churn, or a tightly scoped immediate follow-up.

The main lesson is that Codex subagents are not merely “Claude subagents stored somewhere else.” Their hooks identify children well, but their completion and transcript durability are eventually consistent. The clean abstraction is therefore an authoritative ledger plus reconciliation—not broader transcript discovery.

+## Goal

+

+

It deliberately does not unify the persisted ledgers in this PR: inventory and task records have different lifetimes, and changing their wire format would add migration risk. The simplification will instead target repeated rollout parsing, duplicated secure I/O, Codex-only orchestration checks, and redundant tests—the areas with the best size reduction per unit of risk.

The characterization baseline is green for Codex, session state, and strategy. The integration test is still running because it builds and exercises the real CLI harness; no failures have appeared. After it finishes, I’ll start with the one-pass analyzer because it removes repeated logic without touching persisted state.

- This keeps the actual Codex contract—provisional stop now, terminal rollout confirmation later—while reducing state and tests.

content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `SubagentInventory` is durable session-wide history, so making all inventory count as pending content would be wrong: after a task is checkpointed, its inventory intentionally remains. The correct invariant is narrower—every newly observed stop must create a pending `TaskRecord`.
- A late `SubagentStart` must enrich that placeholder rather than replace it, because replacing could erase completion/evidence if hooks were processed out of order.
- For the race guard, absence and zero are distinct states. A pointer (`nil` = no Codex snapshot, `&0` = valid empty-ledger snapshot) expresses that directly and avoids a second boolean or magic offset.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

I’ll add one focused regression assertion for each finding first, run them red, then make only the production changes needed to turn them green.

“Race-only edge cases” means failures that require two hook processes to interleave in a specific order:

- `SubagentStop` is processed before `SubagentStart`. Previously, that could register the child without creating pending task content, allowing cleanup to discard the session before the delayed start arrived.
- Entire snapshots ledger version `0`, then a child starts before `SaveStep` acquires the state lock. Previously, `0` also meant “no snapshot,” so stale “no children” token coverage could be saved.

A normal Codex smoke run does not reliably create either timing window. The focused tests deliberately control those interleavings.

I didn’t rerun the happy path because the first real session was expensive—roughly 297k total tokens—and the account was showing 97% usage. A second normal run would mostly repeat evidence we already had without testing the actual races.

content.text: I do want to finish the identical real-session rerun before calling this fully validated. The run already proved the core child discovery and aggregate-token path, but it exposed one suspicious gap: the durable per-task record did not retain its file/token evidence. I’m using the Entire context workflow plus systematic debugging to determine whether that is a real implementation defect or merely a timing artifact in how the final checkpoint was inspected.

The discrepancy is reproducible and the cause is now concrete: this Codex child rollout begins with two `task_started` events—an inherited parent-turn marker, then the child’s actual turn. Our validator treats that as an invalid overlap, so it still counts exact child tokens but refuses to attach terminal-turn file/token evidence to the task record. That means the prior smoke validated aggregation and child inventory, but not the full per-task evidence path against today’s real Codex event shape.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The new Codex `history_mode: "paginated"` format intentionally embeds part of the parent transcript inside the child rollout. The child metadata gives the exact cutoff as `subagent_history_start_ordinal`; events below that ordinal are inherited context, while events at or above it belong to the child. The safe fix is therefore to scope all child evidence—terminal turns, files, and token snapshots—to that native cutoff, preserving the existing fail-closed rules inside the true child segment.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

I’ve completed root-cause analysis and am moving into a minimal test-first fix. The regression test will use the real observed shape: inherited parent activity before ordinal 10, followed by the child’s own start, patch, token snapshot, and completion.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The fix is intentionally small: `rolloutLine` now understands Codex’s native ordinal, and `analyzeRollout` filters inherited history before its existing evidence parsers run. This avoids special-casing parent turn IDs or guessing from timestamps. If a paginated rollout cannot be scoped safely because an ordinal is missing or malformed, the parser fails closed instead of attributing uncertain parent activity to the child.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The regression test failed on the old behavior exactly as expected (`parent.txt` leaked into child evidence), and now passes along with the full Codex-agent package. I’m checking formatting, duplication, and the broader lifecycle tests next; then I’ll rebuild and rerun the real Codex happy path against the fixed binary if the account still permits another session.

+
+## Goal
+
+Give GitHub Copilot CLI the same normalized subagent lifecycle used by Claude

+including child metadata, files, transcript when available, and exact token
+usage when Copilot exposes it.

+
+Entire's Copilot adapter reflects an older CLI contract:
+
+- it installs `subagentStop` but not `subagentStart`;
+- it discards `preToolUse` and `postToolUse` payloads;
+- it converts `subagentStop` into `SubagentEnd` with only the parent session ID;
+- shared lifecycle code therefore merges all uncorrelated Copilot children into
+  the task record keyed by the empty string; and
+- its subordinate-session guard recognizes only the historical `toolu_` prefix.
+
+This preserves parent-level file capture but is not per-child tracking.
+
+Current Copilot CLI documentation exposes both `subagentStart` and
+`subagentStop` for YAML-based built-in agents and custom agents. The start
+payload contains `sessionId`, `transcriptPath`, and agent metadata but no
+`agentId`; the stop payload adds `agentId`, `agentType`, and the final response.
+The built-in `general-purpose` agent deliberately emits neither event.

+
+- Rebuilding shared task-record or checkpoint persistence.
+- Guessing child identity from task descriptions, timestamps, directory order,

+- Claiming exact per-child tokens when Copilot exposes only a session aggregate.

+
+Before production changes, run Copilot CLI 1.0.82 or newer in an isolated
+repository with capture-only hooks. Exercise two same-type native subagents,

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Hook timing matters: Copilot invokes `subagentStop` before it appends `subagent.completed`, so a parser that looks only at “completed” records would fail in production despite passing against a finished transcript.
- Fortunately `subagent.started` is already present by stop time and carries both top-level `agentId` and the parent task `toolCallId`. Child tool events also carry that same `agentId`/`parentToolCallId`, which is enough for exact concurrent file attribution.
- Exact per-child token breakdown appears only in `session.shutdown`, which Copilot appends after Entire’s `sessionEnd` hook returns. I will not mislabel `totalTokens` as input or output; task token usage will remain unavailable until Copilot exposes it synchronously or the shared schema gains an honest total-only representation.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The shared lifecycle needed only one narrow extension: a “completion learned without launch” event can create a task record only inside an already-active parent session. Missing or ended state remains a no-op, so late hooks cannot resurrect sessions.
- Copilot’s child files are adapter-derived before dispatch, so shared lifecycle skips both the whole-worktree scan and the generic child-transcript analyzer. That avoids attributing the parent’s or a concurrent child’s files to the wrong task.
- A persisted `transcript_unavailable` bit is important even though it is small: without it, condensation would probe Claude-style `agent-<id>.jsonl` paths and could attach an unrelated file to a Copilot child.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

+# Copilot CLI Native Subagent Tracking Design
+
+## Goal
+
+Give GitHub Copilot CLI durable, per-child task tracking using the shared Entire
+subagent record and checkpoint format. Concurrent children must remain distinct,
+read-only children must still produce records, and ambiguous evidence must fail
+closed rather than merge children together.
+
+## Verified Copilot contract
+
+The contract was captured from the official Copilot CLI 1.0.82 release in an
+isolated repository. Three paid evidence invocations covered:
+
+- two concurrent same-type custom children, one writing and one read-only; and
+- the built-in `general-purpose` child.
+
+Both custom and built-in children emit `subagentStart` and `subagentStop`.
+The start payload contains the parent session ID, parent transcript path, and
+agent name, but no child UUID or task call ID. Two concurrent starts can be
+identical, so start cannot safely create a keyed record.
+
+The stop payload contains:
+
+- the parent UUID as `sessionId`;
+- the parent `events.jsonl` as `transcriptPath`;
+- the child UUID as `agentId`; and
+- `agentType` and `agentName`.
+
+Before the stop hook runs, the parent transcript contains a `subagent.started`
+event with the same top-level child UUID and the parent task `toolCallId`.
+Child tool events carry the same top-level child UUID and a
+`parentToolCallId` equal to that task ID. This is a deterministic join for
+concurrent children and does not depend on descriptions, timestamps, ordering,
+or response text.
+
+Copilot stores all child events in the parent transcript; no standalone child
+transcript exists. `subagent.completed` is appended only after the synchronous
+stop hook returns. Full per-child token breakdown appears later in
+`session.shutdown.agentMetrics`, after the synchronous `sessionEnd` hook
+returns. The adapter therefore cannot honestly attach the child transcript or
+exact token breakdown while handling the child completion.
+
+## Design
+
+### Hooks and upgrades
+
+Entire installs all nine Copilot hook commands, including `subagentStart` and
+`subagentStop`. `subagentStart` is parsed as an observed pass-through signal
+because it lacks a stable child identity. `subagentStop` drives durable capture.
+
+Copilot implements hook freshness reporting. A repository with any Entire-owned
+Copilot hook but without the full current command set is outdated, so an older
+eight-hook installation is surfaced and a reinstall adds exactly the missing
+start hook while preserving user hooks and unknown fields.
+
+### Stop correlation
+
+On `subagentStop`, the adapter:
+
+1. opens Copilot's session store through `agent.SessionStore`;
+2. verifies that `transcriptPath` is exactly the expected
+   `<parent-session>/events.jsonl` beneath that store;
+3. reads it with the rooted no-follow API;
+4. finds the unique `subagent.started` whose top-level `agentId` matches the
+   stop payload; and
+5. uses its `data.toolCallId` as Entire's `ToolUseID`.
+
+Zero or multiple identities produce no normalized event. The adapter does not
+fall back to parsing task result text.
+
+The child file list is the deduplicated `filePaths` from
+`tool.execution_complete` events whose top-level child UUID matches and whose
+`parentToolCallId` equals the correlated task ID. Both the older
+`toolTelemetry.properties` and current `restrictedProperties` locations are
+accepted.
+
+### Shared lifecycle
+
+The normalized stop is a true final `SubagentEnd` marked as a correlated
+completion learned without a launch marker. Shared lifecycle may create its
+task record only if the parent session state already exists and is active.
+Missing or ended parent state is a no-op; no session can be resurrected.
+
+Completion uses only adapter-supplied child files. It skips the whole-worktree
+diff and child-transcript analyzer, both of which would over-attribute parent or
+concurrent-child activity. The normal exactly-once task-record mutation handles
+duplicate stops and preserves one record per `ToolUseID`.
+
+Each record persists `transcript_unavailable: true`. Condensation still writes
+`tasks/<tool-use-id>/task.json` but never probes the generic Claude-style
+`agent-<id>.jsonl` fallback. This prevents an unrelated coincidental file from
+being attached to the Copilot child.
+
+### Tokens and transcript
+
+The task record truthfully reports transcript unavailability and leaves child
+token usage unset. `subagent.completed.totalTokens` is exact but cannot be read
+until the stop hook returns, and the current `TokenUsage` schema has no
+total-only field. Mapping that total to input or output would be incorrect.
+
+Parent-session transcript and token handling remains unchanged. A future
+Copilot hook exposing completed usage, or a future shared total-only token
+field, can enrich the same task record without changing correlation.
+
+## Security and privacy
+
+- Hook-provided paths are never read with unrestricted `os.ReadFile`.
+- Parent transcript reads are confined to Copilot's session store and reject
+  outside paths, wrong layouts, and symlinks.
+- Unsafe session, task, and child IDs remain covered by central lifecycle
+  validation.
+- Logs contain operational IDs and errors, never prompts, responses, or file
+  contents.
+- Evidence fixtures committed to tests contain synthetic structure only.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- A fresh install has one managed start and stop hook; an old install is marked
+  outdated and upgrades idempotently.
+- Custom and `general-purpose` stops resolve to stable non-empty task IDs.
+- Two concurrent same-type children retain disjoint file lists.
+- A read-only child still creates a completed task record.
+- Duplicate, unmatched, missing-parent, and ended-parent stops create no extra
+  record and never resurrect state.
+- Condensation writes task metadata and never fabricates a child transcript.
+- Existing Copilot parent-session behavior and other agents remain unchanged.
+- Focused unit tests, the shared canary, repository checks, and an explicitly
+  authorized real Copilot end-user smoke test pass before push.
*** End Patch";

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The reviewer finding was resolved at the adapter boundary: a child `agentStop` is identifiable because its `sessionId` is the child UUID while `transcriptPath` names the parent UUID. Entire converts that signal into cleanup for the transient child state and never analyzes the parent transcript as the child’s own session.
- This keeps the solution small and avoids a global child registry or scanning every Copilot transcript. The authoritative task record still comes from the parent-scoped `subagentStop`, where both child UUID and parent transcript are explicitly available.

The inline review found one documentation inconsistency—not a behavioral defect: older Copilot releases used `toolu_…` as child lifecycle session IDs, while the current verified release uses child UUIDs and a parent transcript path. The code handles both, but a comment still described the historical form as current. I’m correcting that and documenting the UUID cleanup path so future maintainers don’t accidentally remove either guard.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
There are two separate “phantom session” defenses because Copilot changed shapes across releases. Historical `toolu_…` child hooks can be rejected immediately; current UUID child hooks are indistinguishable at prompt time, so their transient state is retired when `agentStop` reveals that the transcript belongs to a different (parent) session.

That cleanup event intentionally has no transcript reference. This makes the shared lifecycle close the transient state without ever analyzing the parent transcript under the child’s identity.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
